characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Instead of attacking normaly during the Combat phase or making a Giant Attack, a Giant that is engaged in combat with one or more units whose troop type is "regular infantry" or "heavy infantry" may choose to make a "Pick Up And..." attack, nominate an enemy unit of regular or heavy infantry that Giant is engaged in combat with. The unit must inmediatly make an Initiative test.

 - If this test is failed, a victim in picked up by the Giant. What happen next does not bear thinking about, but whatever it is, a single model belong to the target unit is inmediatly removed from play as a casualty.

 - If this test is passed, the warrior manage to duck and dodge away from the Giant´s grasping hands. No one is picked up an the attack has no effect.

 Next, roll a D6 - On a roll of 1-3, the Giant forget what it is doing and makes no further attacks.

 - On a roll of 4+, the Giant attempts to pick up another enemy. The target unit must make another Initiative test.

 This continue until the Giant forget what it is doing and stops making attacks or until the target is destroyed.

 Enemy models removed from play are considered to have been removed from the fighting rank of the enemy unit.

Units of Chaos Marauders and Marauder Horseman have the option to belong to a 'Chaotic Cult':
• A model cannot belong to more than one Chaotic Cult.
• A character with a Mark of Chaos can join a unit belonging to any Chaotic Cult as normal.

**Praising The Gods**
Once per game, during the Command sub-phase of its turn, a unit belonging to a Chaotic Cult may implore its patron for their blessing by making a Leadership test. If this test is passed, until its next Start of Turn sub-phase, all Chaotic Cult models within the unit gain the benefit specified by the specific cult. If this test is failed, the unit's implorations go unheeded.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Three optional sets of 'Winds of Magic' rules plus a new Miscast table, designed to enhance the role of magic - greater power to Wizards at greater risk.

Utilising The Winds Of Magic
The Winds of Magic rules are not compulsory. Before a game begins, the players may agree which of the rules that follow they will use. It is recommended that players use either the rules for Channelling (page 26), or the rules for Arcane Magic (page 27). Sorcerous Ruses (page 30) can be used in conjunction with Channelling or Arcane Magic, or they can be used alone.

Matched Play
If organising a Warhammer: the Old World matched play event, it is recommended that such events allow the use of either Channelling, or Arcane Magic, but not both. Sorcerous Ruses can be used in conjunction with either, or alone.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
If you are using either the rules for Channelling (page 26), or the rules for Arcane Magic (page 27) in your game, you must use the Disastrous Miscast table below, rather than the Miscast table found in the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook. As usual, when a miscast is rolled, the spell is not cast unless the result rolled states otherwise.

The Perils of Magic: Should you wish, especially if you are organising a Warhammer: the Old World matched play event, the Disastrous Miscast table can be used instead of the usual Miscast table even if Channelling and Arcane Magic rules are not in use, making the use of magic far more perilous.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Generating Channelling Dice
Channelling dice are generated before armies are deployed, immediately before spell generation. Choose a Wizard within your army and roll a number of dice, as detailed below. Then gather together that many dice, creating that Wizard's 'Channelling pool'. You may then generate that Wizard's spells, before repeating the process if your army contains any more Wizards. Once generated, each Wizard's Channelling pool should be set safely aside for use throughout the game.

Level 1 Wizards have D3 Channelling dice.

Level 2 Wizards have D3+1 Channelling dice.

Level 3 Wizards have 2D3 Channelling dice.

Level 4 Wizards have 2D3+1 Channelling dice.

Spending Channelling Dice
Wizards can 'spend' Channelling dice in a number of ways throughout the course of a game. There is no limit to how many Channelling dice a Wizard can spend per turn. Each dice spent reduces the number of dice remaining in the Wizard's Channelling pool by one.

Channelled Spells: When randomly generating spells, before discarding one in favour of a signature spell, a Wizard may spend one Channelling dice to re-roll one spell (re-rolling duplicates as normal). You must accept the result of the re-roll, even if the same spell is generated again.

Channelled Casting Rolls*: When making a Casting roll, a Wizard can spend one Channelling dice to channel extra power by rolling an extra D6 and discarding the lowest result.

Channelled Dispel Rolls*: When attempting a Wizardly dispel (including attempts to dispel Remains in Play spells cast during previous turns), a Wizard can spend one Channelling dice to channel extra power. If they do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result.

Channelled Luck: If a Wizard fails a Casting or Dispel roll, they may spend two Channelling dice to re-roll that roll. However, Channelling dice cannot be used to prevent a miscast.

Range Magnification: A Wizard can spend one Channelling dice to increase the range of a spell prior to choosing a target, or to increase their Dispel range prior to attempting a Wizardly dispel. To do so, roll the Channelling dice. The result is the number of inches added to the spell's range, or to the Wizard's Dispel range.

*Note that the effects of a natural double 1 or natural double 6 apply if such a result is rolled on any two of the dice.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Arcane Magic Cards: A deck of 56 cards from which players can draw during the course of a game.

Arcane Magic Table: A 2D6 table listing the same ploys that can be found in the Arcane Magic deck of cards.

Arcane Magic ploys are generated at the start of the game, after the players have generated spells for their Wizards. Each player generates six ploys either by shuffling a deck of Arcane Magic cards and drawing six cards from the top, or by rolling six times on the table. If each player has a deck, each should draw from their own. If only one has a deck, both players may draw from it, taking turns to draw a single card. However, should either player draw more of one card than is allowed on the table, they must replace it, re-shuffle the deck, and draw another. If neither player has a deck, both should roll on the table instead. Whichever method is used, both players must use the same, and ploys must be generated in clear view of your opponent.

A ploy can be used by any model able to use it (i.e., a Wizard, a Dwarf Runesmith, or a model with a Bound spell), and some ploys associated with dispelling can be used when attempting a Fated dispel, as detailed in their descriptions. However, each player can only use one ploy per phase. Once a ploy has been used, it is discarded and cannot be used again for the remainder of the game.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Ruses are generated immediately before spells are generated. Simply choose a Wizard within your army that has purchased a Sorcerous Ruse and roll on the table, repeating the process for each Wizard in your army that has purchased a Ruse. If both players have Wizards that have purchased Ruses, they should take turns rolling on the table, ensuring each roll is made in clear view of the other player. Once a Ruse has been generated, make a note of it, and which Wizard it belongs to.

A Wizard can use their Ruse at any point during the game, as detailed in the Ruse's description. Once a Ruse has been used, whether successfully or not, it cannot be used again.

0-1 per Wizard — 25 points.
Sorcerous Ruses are special abilities available to any Wizard. To represent them, any Wizard in your army may purchase a single roll on the Sorcerous Ruses table for 25 points.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
To craft your own Champion of Chaos, first choose either the Champion of Ruin profile if you are fielding a Warriors of Chaos army (see page 36) or the Chieftain of Ruin profile if you are fielding a Beastman Brayherds army (see page 37). When writing your muster list, you may purchase any optional equipment, magic items or a mount for your chosen Champion as normal. You may always choose a Champion of Ruin or a Chieftain of Ruin to be your army's General, even if they do not have the highest Leadership amongst character models in your army. Once your muster list has been created and shared with your opponent, you then roll on the Chaos Rewards table. Roll on the Chaos Rewards table three times for each Champion, plus any additional rolls purchased when creating your muster list, applying each result to your character in turn.

The Chaos Rewards table and the two profiles (Champion of Ruin, Chieftain of Ruin) are designed with narrative and campaign play in mind, and are not intended for use in Matched Play due to their random nature. However, should an event organiser wish to allow these rules at their tournament, this is perfectly acceptable; it should be clearly stated in the rules pack.

Limite : 1 per player.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
You may use this ploy when you wish to attempt a Wizardly dispel. If you do, you may nominate a single Wizard in your army regardless of their Dispel range and even if they are engaged in combat. Wizards that are fleeing or that have succumbed to Stupidity cannot be nominated.

Limite : 2 per player.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
A model in your army may use this ploy immediately after successfully casting a spell or a Bound spell, even if that spell was dispelled. If they do so, they may immediately cast the spell again, targeting the same unit as before, or a different unit should they wish. This attempt does not count towards how many spells the Wizard can attempt to cast per turn.

Limite : 4 per player.

sharedProfiles.name: Arcane Magic Ploy 5: Twist Of Fate

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: A Wizard in your army may use this ploy after miscasting a spell and rolling on the Miscast table. If they do so, they may immediately re-roll their roll on the Miscast table. However, they must accept the result of the second roll, even if it is worse than the first.

sharedProfiles.name: Arcane Magic Ploy 6: Winds Of Fortune

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: You may use this ploy when attempting a Wizardly dispel or a Fated dispel. If you do so, roll an extra D6 when making the Dispel roll and discard the lowest result. If a double 1 is rolled, the Wizard can avoid being outclassed in the art by discarding one of those dice.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text: You may use this ploy when a Wizard in your army fails a Casting roll, or when they roll a Miscast. If you do so, that Wizard may immediately re-roll the Casting roll. Alternatively, this ploy can be used to re-roll a failed Casting roll when a model in your army attempts to cast a Bound spell.

If you do so, that Wizard may immediately re-roll the Dispel roll. Alternatively, this ploy can be used to re-roll a failed Dispel roll when you attempt a Fated dispel.

Limite : 4 per player.

Limite : 2 per player.

Limite : 1 per player.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
The first time a Wizard is reduced to zero Wounds, they may use this Ruse immediately before they are removed from play. If they do so, roll a D6:

1-3: The Ruse has not paid off and the Wizard must face their fate.

4+: The Wizard immediately recovers a single lost Wound.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
When an enemy Wizard casts a spell, a Wizard may use this Ruse instead of attempting a Wizardly dispel.

Both Wizards roll a D6. The Wizard using this Ruse adds their Level of Wizardry to their roll, whilst the enemy Wizard adds their Toughness.

Enemy Wizard's result is higher: The Ruse has failed and the spell is cast.

Draw: The Ruse was partially successful and the spell is dispelled.

This Wizard's result is higher: The spell is dispelled and the enemy Wizard loses a single Wound. This Wound cannot be recovered by a Regeneration save.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
When an enemy Wizard casts a spell, a Wizard may use this Ruse instead of attempting a Wizardly dispel.

Both Wizards roll a D6. Each Wizard then divides their Level of Wizardry by 2 (rounding fractions up) and adds the result to their roll.

Enemy Wizard's result is higher: The Ruse has failed and the spell is cast.

Draw: The Ruse was partially successful and the spell is dispelled.

This Wizard's result is higher: The spell is flayed from the enemy Wizard's mind. The spell is dispelled and the enemy Wizard is unable to attempt to cast it again for the remainder of the game.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
When an enemy Wizard casts a spell, a Wizard may use this Ruse instead of attempting a Wizardly dispel.

Both Wizards roll a D6. The Wizard using this Ruse adds their Level of Wizardry to their roll, whilst the enemy Wizard adds their Initiative.

Enemy Wizard's result is higher: The Ruse has failed and the spell is cast.

Draw: The Ruse was partially successful and the spell is dispelled.

This Wizard's result is higher: The spell is reflected back upon its caster. The spell is resolved against its caster and their unit, exactly as if they were the target of the spell.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
When an enemy Wizard casts a spell, a Wizard may use this Ruse instead of attempting a Wizardly dispel.

The Wizard using this Ruse rolls 2D6 and adds their Level of Wizardry, whilst the enemy Wizard rolls a D6 and adds their Leadership.

Enemy Wizard's result is higher: The Ruse has failed and the spell is cast.

Draw: The Ruse was partially successful and the spell is dispelled.

This Wizard's result is higher: The spell is dispelled, along with any other enemy spells currently in play.

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
The spell is automatically dispelled with no Dispel roll required. If the spell was cast with a perfect invocation, the Wizard may attempt to dispel it as normal by making a Dispel roll. If they roll a natural double 6, the spell is dispelled. In addition, the next time this Wizard makes a Casting roll after using this Ruse, they may unleash the power of the consumed spell by rolling an extra D6 and discarding the lowest result. If a double 1 is rolled, a miscast can be avoided by discarding one of those dice.

When an enemy Wizard casts a spell, a Wizard may use this Ruse instead of attempting a Wizardly dispel.

selectionEntries.name: The Cult of the Bloodied Hound

profiles.name: The Cult of the Bloodied Hound

characteristics.name: Description
characteristics.$text:
Once per game, during the Command sub-phase of its turn, a unit belonging to a Chaotic Cult may implore it's patron for their blessing by making a Leadership test. If this test is passed, until its next Start of Turn sub-phase, all Chaotic Cult models within the unit gain the following benefit. If this test is failed, the unit's implorations go unheeded:
Models belonging to this Chaotic Cult gain a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic
